summary: The design can reuse the existing lifecycle dual-emit mechanism, but it needs explicit global-registry wiring, a cost-to-response propagation contract, and stronger tenant/metadata coverage. The largest operational risk is treating fire-and-forget Redis Pub/Sub as durable accounting telemetry.

suggestions.title: Add an explicit global EventBus configuration lifecycle
suggestions.rationale: EventRegistry accepts an EventBus, but get_global_registry() lazily creates one without a bus and exposes no public configuration hook. Configure the host-owned bus before bot/client creation, register the four forwarding subscriptions, return subscription IDs, and drain/unsubscribe them during shutdown; account for the global registry being stored in a ContextVar.

suggestions.title: Use one dedicated, idempotent bus-forwarding provider
suggestions.rationale: forward_to_bus is per subscription, so registering multiple forwarders or passing the same EventBus to both bot registries and the global registry can duplicate every event. Use one provider with exactly four narrow subscriptions, retain its IDs, and make repeated setup/reload a no-op or explicit reconfiguration.

suggestions.title: Make origin cost calculation independent of local OTel setup
suggestions.rationale: CostCalculator instances are currently created separately by bootstrap.py and setup.py, while AbstractClient does not receive one. If bus forwarding is enabled while local observability is disabled, cost_usd will otherwise remain absent. Introduce one process-scoped calculator/configuration source, resolve the same provider mapping used by subscribers, compute once when constructing AfterClientCallEvent, and have recorders, metrics, and traces read event.cost_usd.

suggestions.title: Define how origin cost reaches AgentTalk persistence
suggestions.rationale: AgentTalk receives an AIMessage, not the lifecycle event, and event-bus forwarding is asynchronous. AIMessage currently carries usage and metadata but no cost field, so the handler cannot persist cost_usd without recalculating it. Propagate the already-computed value into response metadata at the client/origin boundary, then make AgentTalk copy it rather than calling CostCalculator again.

suggestions.title: Use one tenant ContextVar and bind it on every ask path
suggestions.rationale: The current tenant carrier is the skills-only _skill_tenant, and BaseBot binds it only when the skill mixin is present. Add one generic current_tenant carrier with token-based nesting/reset, make skills.tenancy delegate to it instead of maintaining a second variable, and bind it for every ask() and ask_stream() invocation so client and invoke events see the same value.

suggestions.title: Resolve and strip AgentTalk tenant input once
suggestions.rationale: ChatHandler already removes client-supplied tenant before calling resolve_request_tenant, but AgentTalk currently neither resolves a tenant nor strips request data. Resolve with the existing scope helper, discard client input, pass the server value to both bot.ask and the _handle_stream_response/bot.ask_stream path, and ensure background save tasks receive explicit metadata rather than reading a reset ContextVar.

suggestions.title: Add user and session attribution to terminal invoke events
suggestions.rationale: The brief claims usage events carry user_id/session_id, but AfterInvokeEvent and InvokeFailedEvent currently do not; only BeforeInvokeEvent has those fields, and BeforeInvokeEvent is explicitly excluded from forwarding. Without adding the fields or defining a reliable trace-join contract, external consumers cannot produce per-user invoke failure/error attribution.

suggestions.title: Sanitize failed-event payloads before external forwarding
suggestions.rationale: ClientCallFailedEvent and InvokeFailedEvent contain error_message, and EventRegistry forwards event.to_dict() wholesale. Provider exception strings can contain request fragments, credentials, or other sensitive data; the telemetry requirement needs error rate, not necessarily raw messages. Define an allowlisted/sanitized bus payload or explicitly document and test the privacy contract.

suggestions.title: Audit non-AbstractClient event emitters
suggestions.rationale: The Claude Code dispatcher constructs AfterClientCallEvent and ClientCallFailedEvent directly, outside AbstractClient._emit_after_call. Those paths can bypass the new origin cost calculation and tenant/user context capture. Route all direct emitters through a shared event builder or explicitly exclude and test these out-of-process coding-agent events.

suggestions.title: Do not promise durable accounting over Redis Pub/Sub
suggestions.rationale: The EventRegistry bus handoff is fire-and-forget, and navigator_eventbus RedisPubSubBackend documents fan-out as at-most-once and unpersisted. This can undercount BigQuery cost/tokens during worker crashes or Redis outages. Either use a durable transport/outbox for accounting or state the loss semantics and expose dropped/failed-publish telemetry.

suggestions.title: Test exact-once forwarding, attribution, and persistence together
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests cover registry dual-emit and client-to-global forwarding, but the feature needs a cross-layer matrix: default-off behavior, four exact channels, one bus publish per event, slow/failing bus isolation, nested tenant reset, one CostCalculator call observed by all three subscribers, both AgentTalk save_turn paths, and preservation of metadata in hot and cold storage.

suggestions.title: Preserve custom metadata in ChatStorage’s Redis tier
suggestions.rationale: ChatStorage.save_turn accepts metadata and includes it in the assistant ChatMessage/DynamoDB payload, but its Redis ConversationTurn is rebuilt with only output_mode, model, provider, and response_time_ms. Passing usage, cost_usd, tenant, and agent from AgentTalk will therefore be lost on hot-tier reads unless the supplied metadata is merged into that ConversationTurn metadata.
